title: Hugging Face proposes Model Integration Contracts for testing AI models
excerpt: The new standard uses shrunk model fixtures to catch regressions in the Transformers library before they reach the main branch.
bodyHtml:
Hugging Face announced a proposed standard called Model Integration Contracts (MIC) on November 3, 2026, to improve testing for the Transformers library. The system uses shrunk model fixtures, which are small versions of real model checkpoints with fewer layers, to run integration tests on CPU hardware.

A Model Integration Contract consists of a pinned fixture, a runnable Markdown usage path, and human-reviewed baseline outputs. The company developed the tmic command-line interface to help users draft contracts and record baselines. This tool allows developers to measure candidate baselines on both CPU and GPU runs.

The recipe for creating these fixtures involves four steps: shrinking the configuration, preserving preprocessing, building and validating weights, and freezing the final record. The process ensures that the model responds to inputs and maintains finite outputs, loss, and gradients.

As of November 1, 2026, the MIC job in the Transformers continuous integration system reports failures without blocking pull requests. The company is currently evaluating how many real bugs the system catches and how often it generates false alarms before deciding if the process should block future updates.
